question.text: An NRI based in the USA wishes to trade in the Indian equity market. Which of the following statements about the PINS (Portfolio Investment NRI Scheme) account is CORRECT?

answer.text: An NRI can maintain multiple PINS accounts with different brokers simultaneously
A PINS account can be linked to either an NRE or NRO account as per the NRI's free preference
An NRI can route PINS investments through a single authorised dealer, with an NRE(PIS) account for repatriable transactions and an NRO(PIS) account for non-repatriable transactions
A PINS account is optional for NRIs who only wish to invest in mutual funds and not in direct equities

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the PINS framework an NRI/PIO can have one PINS account with one NRE(PIS) account for transactions on a repatriation basis and one NRO(PIS) account for transactions on a non-repatriation basis, routed through a single authorised dealer; the NRI trading account is then linked to these NRE and NRO accounts. The Trap: The PINS account is not free-form linkable to either NRE or NRO at the client's preference, and it is not restricted to NRE alone — the workbook ties NRE(PIS) specifically to the repatriable leg and NRO(PIS) to the non-repatriable leg. Note: Mutual fund investments by NRIs can be done outside the PINS route; PINS is specifically for portfolio investment in listed equities.
